claims.explanation: Isoxsuprine is a beta-adrenergic agonist that also inhibits CDK1, and its selective killing likely reflects dependence on adrenergic signaling and/or CDK1 activity rather than a single lineage. Lines with TP53 pathway loss combined with intact ARID1A/SMARCA4 chromatin-remodeling function appear enriched among sensitive lines, while ARID1A-mutant or PBRM1-mutant lines are often less affected, suggesting that chromatin-remodeling status modulates the response. The virtual-cell signature (adrenergic-receptor-antagonist similarity, CDK1 inhibition) supports a mechanism involving beta-adrenergic/CDK1-linked proliferation and survival pathways.

features.basis: TP53 mutations are highly enriched in the most-killed lines and rare in the least-affected lines
ARID1A mutations appear in several least-affected lines and are absent from most sensitive lines
SMARCA4 mutations occur in least-affected lines (NCIH1793, NCIH1703) but not in the sensitive set
PBRM1 mutations are present in least-affected lines (KMRC1, NCIH1793)
Isoxsuprine inhibits CDK1 (IC50 2.9 uM), so high CDK1 expression may increase dependence
Isoxsuprine is an ADRB2 agonist; receptor expression could mediate selective signaling effects
KRAS mutations are common in the sensitive lines (NCIH1792, SW480, NCIH1339, LS1034, RD)
BRAF mutations appear in sensitive lines (AM38, IGR37) but also in some resistant lines, so weaker evidence
NF1 mutations are present in several sensitive lines (RD, LCLC103H) but also in resistant lines
PTEN mutations occur in sensitive lines (TE4, U118MG, NCIH1339) but also in resistant lines
STK11 mutations appear in sensitive lines (TE4, NCIH1623) but also in resistant G361
SF3B1 mutations are enriched in least-affected lines (TE10, UO31, NCIH1703) and also in some sensitive lines
